MN-2025-HF4133.policyArea: Housing and Housing Finance Agency, Insurance, Police and Peace Officers
MN-2025-HF4133.aiSummary: Minnesota law now says homeowners insurance cannot leave out coverage for certain property damage caused by a peace officer using chemical irritants, smoke screens, or diversionary devices when the homeowner is owed just compensation. It also lets the homeowner choose the repair contractor and, if needed, an industrial hygienist to check and fix the damage. The law takes effect January 1, 2027, and applies to policies offered, issued, or renewed on or after that date.

MN-2025-SF3602.policyArea: Death, Funerals, and Cemeteries, Legal Proceedings, Trusts
MN-2025-SF3602.aiSummary: The law creates rules for electronic estate planning papers in Minnesota, such as trusts, powers of attorney, advance directives, and some body-disposition forms. It defines terms like electronic record, electronic signature, and electronic presence, and says these papers can be handled electronically unless the document says no. It took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF3210.aiSummary: The law adds a rule that not trying to work out a reasonable accommodation for a person with a disability may count as unfair discrimination. It applies to employment, housing, public accommodations, public services, and education. The law took effect on August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF4063.policyArea: Education and Education Department, Safety, Traffic Regulations
MN-2025-HF4063.aiSummary: The law changes rules for school buses in Minnesota. It lets school buses be used for driver training, requires a USDOT number for school bus tracking, and changes first aid kit rules for newer buses, with all type III buses required to have the newer kit by January 1, 2030. It also limits some school bus warning equipment on public roads when a bus is used by a licensed commercial driver training school.

MN-2025-HF1606.aiSummary: This law prohibits websites, apps, and similar services from letting users alter or make images or videos to show fake nude or sexual body parts of a real, identifiable person. It also bans advertising or promoting services that do this, and it lets the person shown in the image sue for damages, court orders, and legal fees. The attorney general can enforce the law, and it takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF1410.policyArea: Corrections and Corrections Department, Police and Peace Officers, Public Safety Department
MN-2025-HF1410.aiSummary: The law changes discipline rules for correctional officers and peace officers in Minnesota. It adds steps for written complaints, witness lists, access to reports, recording of statement sessions, and the right to have a union representative or lawyer present. It also lets an officer seek actual damages, costs, and attorney fees if a state or local agency breaks these rules. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-HF4252.aiSummary: This law changes several higher education rules in Minnesota. It updates student aid reports, limits some student fees for athletic facilities, allows a land lease for Rochester Community and Technical College, and changes rules for American Indian Scholars, private career schools, and some private and out-of-state public colleges. It also expands paid blood donation leave for Minnesota State employees, requires priority registration for pregnant and parenting students, and includes money for higher education.
